marketMood: Higher-for-longer rates meet a dual central-bank tightening day — the Fed's first hike since 2023 collides with a near-certain BOJ move, while Brent above $100 on Saudi pipeline closure keeps energy and risk sentiment in tension.

US August Industrial Production & Capacity Utilization

topStories.headline: Fed Hikes 25bps to 3.75%–4%, First Rate Increase Since 2023; More Tightening Signalled
topStories.summary: The FOMC voted 12-0 on September 16 to raise the fed funds target to 3.75%–4%, the first increase in more than three years, with Chairman Kevin Warsh citing persistent oil-driven inflation and projecting at least one more hike this year.
topStories.marketImpact: S&P 500 sold off 0.45% on Wednesday then recovered 1.14% Thursday; 10Y yield spiked to 5.04% ↑ before settling at 4.93% ↓; 'higher for longer' narrative pressures rate-sensitive equities

topStories.headline: Saudi Arabia's Critical East-West Oil Pipeline Shut After Houthi Drone Attacks
topStories.summary: Saudi Arabia closed its 7 million barrel-per-day East-West Petroline after multiple drone strikes launched from Iraq; Houthis also seized Yemen's Perim Island, tightening their grip on the Bab el-Mandeb Strait.
topStories.marketImpact: Brent briefly topped $105 before easing to ~$103.83 today ↓ on Saudi restoration hopes; WTI ~$101 ↓; energy stocks ↑; supply disruption risk 'watch'

topStories.headline: Bank of Japan Concludes Two-Day Meeting Today; Rate Hike to 1.25% Near-Certain
topStories.summary: All 52 surveyed economists expect the BOJ to raise its benchmark rate by 25bps to 1.25% — the highest since 1995 — as Japan's inflation persists near 2% and yen weakness remains elevated; Governor Ueda stated hikes are on the table at every meeting.
topStories.marketImpact: Yen ↑ (USD/JPY ~155); Japan 10-year JGB yield nudged above 3% for first time since 1996; Nikkei and rate-sensitive Japanese financials 'watch'

topStories.headline: Hang Seng Falls 0.8% After Fed Hike; Hong Kong Faces Multiple Market Headwinds
topStories.summary: The Hang Seng Index fell to 24,537.30 on Thursday as the Fed rate hike and forward guidance rattled Hong Kong markets, with the Hang Seng Tech Index losing 0.5% amid ongoing concerns over AI trade momentum and share lock-up expirations.
topStories.marketImpact: 0700.HK (Tencent) ↓; 9988.HK (Alibaba) ↓; foreign capital repositioning weighs; state buying supports mainland CSI 300 but HK less insulated

topStories.headline: Beijing $1B Land Auction Collapses With Single Bidder; Property Sector Stress Deepens
topStories.summary: A Beijing land auction valued at over $1 billion attracted only one bidder and was subsequently cancelled, underscoring the continued weakness in developer appetite even as authorities attempt to stabilise China's five-year property downturn.
topStories.marketImpact: China property developer stocks ↓; local government fiscal strain grows; stimulus expectations building — watch for PBOC or fiscal policy response

topStories.headline: US 10-Year Treasury Yield Touches 5% — Highest Since 2007 — Before Post-Fed Relief
topStories.summary: The US 10-year Treasury yield rose as high as 5.04% on Tuesday, its first time above that threshold since October 2007, driven by Fed rate hike expectations and elevated oil prices; it eased to 4.93% Thursday after the Fed delivered its move.
topStories.marketImpact: Rate-sensitive sectors (real estate, utilities, long-duration growth) ↓; 30-year yield at 5.28% ↑; bond market pricing one more Fed hike before year-end

topStories.headline: Tech Leads Post-Fed Recovery; Nasdaq Rebounds 1.69% as AI Infrastructure Bets Return
topStories.summary: US equities staged a broad recovery Thursday as bond yields and oil retreated, with Nasdaq leading; AI safety concerns lifted cybersecurity names (Palo Alto Networks +4%, CrowdStrike +5.4%) while Nvidia recovered from a mid-week 3% decline.
topStories.marketImpact: Nasdaq +1.69% ↑; NVDA ↑; PANW ↑; CRWD ↑; semiconductor infrastructure spending narrative intact despite AI safety debate

topStories.headline: Japan's Foreign Reserves Drop at Fastest Pace on Record as Yen Intervention Costs Mount
topStories.summary: Japan's foreign reserves fell 6.18% in August to $1.207 trillion — the steepest monthly decline since records began in 2000 — after Tokyo spent a record ¥15.4 trillion ($98bn) defending the yen in a coordinated effort with the US.
topStories.marketImpact: Yen intervention capacity 'watch'; USD/JPY ~155 ahead of BOJ decision; today's expected BOJ hike adds further yen support ↑; JGB market volatile
